message.reasoning:
We need to fix compilation errors. The test class has many redundant @Before methods and missing imports for JUnit5? They used JUnit4 annotations (@Before, @Test) but also some commented JUnit5. The class is package-private, but test runner didn't find tests because maybe JUnit4 not recognized? Actually they have @Test from org.junit.* which is JUnit4. However they have multiple @Before methods, which is okay but they all run, overriding numericIndicator etc. But the test methods refer to numericIndicator, values, simpleIndicator which are set in setUp (the last @Before). However there are duplicate @Before methods causing ambiguous? JUnit4 allows multiple @Before, they all run in order of declaration. The earlier setUpBeforeEach is not annotated (commented). So fine.

But the test class references MockBarSeries which is not imported nor defined; but those lines are commented out. So compile should be fine.

Potential issue: NumericIndicator.min(Number) may throw IllegalArgumentException for NaN or infinite; tests expect that. Implementation may not throw; but we cannot modify library; we need to adapt test to actual behavior? However we cannot change library. The failing test count is zero because no tests were discovered. That suggests the test class is not recognized as a test because it uses JUnit5 runner? The test runner shows JUnit Jupiter and Vintage present, but 0 tests found. Possibly because the test class is not public. In JUnit4, test classes must be public. The class is package-private (default). So JUnit4 will ignore it. Need to make class public. Also need a public no-arg constructor (default). So change class declaration to public class NumericIndicator_min_2_Test.

Also need to import org.junit.Before, org.junit.Test etc; they already imported org.junit.* which includes them.

Thus fix: make class public.

Also there are duplicate @Before methods which may cause reinitialization but fine.

Let's output corrected code with public class.
